title: Hands-off Action Telemetry: SDK Playbook (draft)
body:
Summary:

This sketch is a pragmatic playbook for a "hands-off" SDK surface that makes it easy for product teams to get rich action-level telemetry from Hosted API streaming + tool-calling flows without forcing heavyweight contract changes on integrators. Focus: streaming partials, tool handshake observability, structured action envelopes, and low-friction developer ergonomics.

Problem we're solving:
- Customers and internal teams lack consistent signals for partial/committed action behavior during streaming sessions (e.g., when tool-calls are queued/hedged/aborted).
- Current SDKs surface call/response but do not capture action lifecycle (prefetch, emit-partial, tool-resolve, commit) in a way that connects traces, costs, and user-visible outputs.
- Debugging regressions (broken tool calls or silent fallback to simpler model) requires manual instrumentation and ad-hoc logs.

Goals (measurable):
- G1: Provide an SDK-level telemetry envelope that records action lifecycles end-to-end with <100ms overhead for hot paths.
- G2: Enable sampled full-trace correlation between client SDK, Hosted API (request id), and tool execution sidecar.
- G3: Create a compact structured action format (stable v1) so backend evals can parse action fidelity regressions automatically.
- G4: Design SDK ergonomics so adoption requires <= 2 code changes for typical embedders.

Success metrics:
- Adoption: 25% of new Hosted API customers opt into the telemetry envelope during onboarding in Q2.
- Troubleshooting: mean time to root cause for tool-call failures drops 40% in pilot accounts.
- Observability: ability to detect partial-to-final mismatches from telemetry in <5 minutes for 90% of sampled sessions.

Target scenarios / user stories:
- Mobile chat client: wants to show "thinking", then a tool result, then final answer; needs to correlate partials to tool latencies to tune prefetch.
- Marketplace integrator: wants to detect when a tool was hedged (fast fallback to local handler) and how often fallbacks produce degraded structured output.
- Internal infra: SRE wants a low-volume sampled trace that links SDK session id -> Hosted API request id -> tool invocation id -> tool response code.

Key constraints & principles:
- Backwards compatible: default SDK behavior unchanged unless opt-in.
- Low foot-print: telemetry envelope is compact (base64 or JSONL) and supports sampling.
- Privacy-first: PII redaction hooks; KMS-aware for sampled payload capture.
- Developer ergonomics: minimal API surface changes; clear migration path.

Proposed SDK surface (high level):
- TelemetryManager (opt-in) with three primitives: annotateAction(action_id, metadata), recordEvent(action_id, event_type, meta), finalizeAction(action_id, resultSummary).
- Action Token: opaque id returned by SDK when an action begins; passed to client UI or local toollets to correlate UI progress.
- Opt-in flags: enable_action_telemetry=true, telemetry_sampling_rate=0.01 (default 1%).
- Minimal code example (pseudo):
  const tok = Telemetry.beginAction({type: 'search_tool', sessionId: s});
  Telemetry.recordEvent(tok, 'prefetch_start');
  // call Hosted API streaming generator with {action_token: tok}
  Telemetry.finalizeAction(tok, {outcome: 'tool_resolved', toolLatencyMs: 420});

Streaming semantics (edge cases we must handle):
- Partial emissions: SDK should map each partial chunk to an action token when available; if SDK cannot, it should tag chunk as "orphan-partial" with request id.
- Resume/reconnect: when session resumes, previously started actions should be re-associated by token when server includes token in resumed frames.
- Abort/timeout: recordEvent(action_id, 'aborted', {reason}) and optionally attach last-partial payload if sampled.

Tool-calling contract notes:
- Idempotency: action_token must be idempotent for retries. Backend ensures tool-call dedupe keyed by (action_token, model_version).
- Hedging & fallbacks: when a tool hedges (multiple backends), Telemetry should capture which diverged and which became authoritative.
- Structured tool response: expect tool response as {action_token, status, payload_schema, summary}. SDK will present same shape to downstream code and include telemetry on status transitions.

Structured output format (proposal v1):
- envelope: {version: "1", action_id: string, phase: one_of('prefetch','partial','tool_wait','tool_result','commit','abort'), meta: {...}, payload: {format: 'json-schema-v1' | 'text', data: ...}}
- Example: {"version":"1","action_id":"a-42","phase":"tool_result","meta":{"tool":"search-v2","latency_ms":200},"payload":{"format":"json-schema-v1","data":{"results":[{"id":"doc:34","score":0.92}]}}} 
- The payload format is intentionally lightweight so automatic regression tools can diff JSON payloads across model versions.

Observability strategy:
- Events to capture (per action): start, prefetch_done, partial_emitted, tool_invoked, tool_responded, commit, abort, sample_payload (optional).
- Correlation keys: client_session_id, sdk_action_token, hosted_request_id, trace_id (W3C), tool_invocation_id.
- Sampling: reservoir sampling per-session with decay policy; default 1% but can be raised for internal accounts.
- Export sinks: primary -> Redwood telemetry pipeline (low-volume), secondary -> customer-provided endpoint (if configured).
- Developer-friendly UI hooks: Telemetry.on('interest', callback) to allow app to toggle higher fidelity for problematic UX flows.

Operational considerations:
- Storage: sampled payloads stored for 14 days by default, redact PII per policy; customers can opt-in to longer retention via enterprise settings.
- Cost: sampling reduces cost; compute overhead kept <0.1% tokens for common chat patterns.
- Security: sampled payloads encrypted client-side if enable_local_kms=true.

Migration & compatibility:
- Default SDKs: no opt-in changes. Telemetry opt-in via feature flag or client configuration.
- Server fallback: Hosted API will echo action_token where available, but will handle missing tokens by generating server-side tokens and mapping them back to SDK when possible.

Open questions (needs triage):
- Q1: Exact wire format for embedded action_token in streaming frames (compact vs explicit JSON field).
- Q2: How to ensure tool sidecar exposure of invocation id without forcing customers to change tool integration? (suggest: automatic wrapper lambda that returns tool_invocation_id).
- Q3: PII redaction rules — do we offer default regex or allow customer-supplied sanitizer hooks?

Next steps / short roadmap (recommended):
- Week 0–1: Align on action envelope v1 (engineering + SRE).
- Week 2: Prototype SDK opt-in with in-memory sampling and local dev hook; demo with two pilot customers.
- Week 3–4: Implement server echo of action_token in streaming frames + trace correlation (lightweight).
- Week 5: Integrate telemetry export to Redwood pipeline; build small UI in Console to view sampled action traces.

Sprint TODOs (owner tags):
- Aisha: write minimal wire spec and publish to confluence (draft).
- Liam: prototype TelemetryManager in JS SDK (POC).
- María: design Console view for sampled action traces and payload diff tool.
- Owen: draft server-side dedupe semantics and idempotency note for tool infra.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could support a "telemetry-lite" header that only emits events without sampled payloads for extremely low-volume customers.
- Consider offering a small CLI to pull sampled traces for offline debugging.

If this looks reasonable I will turn the envelope proposal into a concise PRD and flag engineering for a two-week spike.

End.
